title: ARES Net Relay: "Spruce Hill Under Water, Kids Missing"

fields.centerName: EOC Radio Room, Kellerton (with 911 Backup Consoles)
fields.channel: ARES 2-Meter Net, relayed to EOC Radio Room

lines.text: Net control to EOC, priority traffic.
EOC radio room, go ahead with your priority traffic.
A station at the north end of Spruce Hill relays that the Spruce Hill assembly area is under water and some of the school kids are missing. Second-hand, I can't raise the original station.
Copy, Spruce Hill under water, students missing, second-hand. Who was the original station, and what time did they report it?
Unknown. It came in weak, a mobile, no tactical call given, maybe five minutes ago. I've called them three times. Nothing. Net control standing by.

Supervisor, Console 2. That's nine parent calls in four minutes. 'School kids missing at Spruce Hill?' 'Where do I pick up my child?' 'Is Marlow Coast High School open?' One caller says it's all over the parents' group, the hill flooded. What do I tell them?

fields.voiceStyle: Net control: older male amateur operator, steady, procedural, slightly clipped by a weak repeater. EOC radio operator: calm woman, measured. Console 2: younger telecommunicator, fast and strained, heavy call load around her.

instructorNote: This is a red herring. It tests whether the 911 Supervisor holds a second-hand report as unverified and passes it to Field Ops, and whether Field Ops checks it with the closest unit or the principal's radio before anyone repeats it. Once players check, tell them Spruce Hill is dry and all 210 students and 28 staff are accounted for. Then watch for the PIO to release one verified reunification message: students are safe, reunification is at Marlow Coast High School, and parents must not drive into the zone. The PIO should also ask ARES net control to flag the original report as false.
